sections.html:
Multnomah County is Oregon's smallest county by area, 466 square miles with 34 of them water, and Portland, the seat and biggest city, sits inside it. The county hugs the Columbia's south bank, and the Willamette cuts through. Population was 815,428 in 2020. Other cities include Gresham, Troutdale, Fairview, Wood Village and Maywood Park.

Street addresses carry one of six sector labels (N, NE, NW, S, SE, SW), with the Willamette dividing east from west and Burnside dividing north from south. West side hillsides bring extra scrutiny: a 2014 report named over 7,000 Portland locations as high risk for landslides and soil liquefaction in a big earthquake. Expect a buyer's lender to ask about retaining walls, drainage and insurance.

Winters in Portland run cool and wet, about 37 inches of precipitation across roughly 157 rainy days. On older houses, inspectors focus on roofs, drainage and foundations. An as-is sale skips the repair haggling, yet you still must disclose what you know.

The city dropped single-family-only zoning in 2021, so a big lot may support more than one home. Ask a planner.

This year's deadline was Monday, November 16, since the 15th is a Sunday. Statements went out by October 25, about 300,000 of them counting value notices.

Full paymentNovember 16, 20263 percent

Anything under $40 is due in full in November. Late balances grow by 1.3333 percent a month (16 percent a year), and a bounced check adds $25. Extensions and interest waivers are outside the county's legal authority.

Options: online, phone (503-988-2225), mail (P.O. Box 2716, Portland, OR 97208-2716), the counter at Suite 175 of 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd, or the 24-hour check drop box outside. For scale, countywide taxes and special assessments in 2026 come to $2.602 billion, up about 3.5 percent from 2025.

sections.h2: How values and tax limits work
sections.html:
Everything begins with real market value, the assessor's January 1 estimate. The rate is then applied to assessed value, the smaller of that figure and maximum assessed value. Measure 50 keeps yearly growth on existing property at or below 3 percent.

Measure 5 adds its own caps: $5 per $1,000 of real market value for schools, $10 per $1,000 for general government. Where the two calculations differ, the gap is compression, and the TaxGraph tool shows a property's compression history.

  • Each district gets its own lines for education, general government and bonds.
  • Renovations made by January 1 can raise the value on the next statement.
  • A yellow statement means a lender or deferral program requested the bill.

Petition the Property Values Appeals Board by December 31, by postmark or hand delivery. County commissioners appoint private citizens to the panel, which works apart from the assessor.

  1. Choose the right form: real property, personal property or late-filing penalty.
  2. Pay $30 per account to Multnomah County.
  3. Mail it to PO Box 5007, Portland, OR 97208-5007, or drop it at 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd, Suite 175. Email and fax do not work, and a postage meter stamp is not a postmark.
  4. Watch for a hearing notice, sent 5 to 10 days ahead. Hearings take place from February through April 15.
  5. Present your case in about 5 minutes, and expect a decision the same day.

Good evidence includes a recent sale between unrelated parties, a fee appraisal near January 1, comparable sales, written repair estimates or contractor costs. The board cannot reduce the 3 percent increase over the prior year's assessed value, except for an exception such as new improvements. It also cannot weigh hardship or hear arguments about tax rates. The written order normally comes within a week, and a further appeal goes to the Oregon Tax Court.

A tax lien attaches on July 1. Foreclosure of real property becomes possible when the earliest delinquency is three years old. By the county's example, 2021 taxes turned delinquent on May 16, 2022, and the property could be foreclosed in May 2025.

  • Interest accrues at 1.3333 percent monthly after each 15th.
  • Every payment is applied to the oldest tax first.
  • Foreclosure notices go to the owner with the payment timeline.
  • On business property the county issues a Notice of Intent to Warrant and then a recorded warrant, which can lead to garnishment or seizure.

A payment plan may head off escalated collection. Request one through the online form or call Tax Collections at 503-988-3334. Owing several years? Seek advice early, because the clock follows the earliest unpaid year.

sections.h2: How deeds get recorded when a house sells
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the county Recorder, inside the Division of Assessment, Recording and Taxation. Title companies usually send sales electronically, and the daily cutoff is 4:15 p.m.

Paper filers can mail to PO Box 5007, use the 24-hour drop box at the Multnomah Building, or visit Suite 175 at 501 SE Hawthorne Blvd on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Type on recorded documents must be 10-point or larger since January 1, 2024. Staff cannot offer legal advice or fill in forms, and a document that cannot be recorded comes back with an explanation.

sections.h2: Step by step for a seller
sections.html:
1. Find your statement and note which payment option you chose and what has been paid.
  2. Call Customer Service at 503-988-2225 and ask for the full balance, including any older years.
  3. If the value looks too high, decide before December 31 whether to petition the board, and gather a recent sale, an appraisal or contractor estimates.
  4. If you owe several years, ask Tax Collections at 503-988-3334 about a payment plan before foreclosure notices start.
  5. Tell the title company about every lien, so recording and payoff go through in one visit.

Drop-box payments for checks are available around the clock at the Hawthorne Blvd address, which helps when the office is closed.

Hand your title company the latest statement and any lien notices. Back taxes come out of the sale money, oldest year first, and Customer Service at 503-988-2225 can give a payoff figure. If you are relocating for work and need a firm closing date, a cash offer with no lender conditions is easier to promise on a house that needs repairs. Plan ahead for the November due date if your closing is close to it, and decide in the contract who pays. A cash buyer can often work around such dates, and skips lender appraisal delays as well.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 Multnomah County tax deadline?
faqs.a: Monday, November 16, 2026, since the 15th is a Sunday. Full payment saves 3 percent and two-thirds saves 2 percent, while three equal installments earn nothing.

faqs.q: What does a Multnomah County value appeal cost?
faqs.a: $30 per account, paid to Multnomah County. Postmark or deliver the petition by December 31. Email and fax are refused.

faqs.q: What interest does Multnomah County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: 1.3333 percent a month, or 16 percent a year. The county cannot waive it or push back the deadline.

faqs.q: When can Multnomah County foreclose on unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: After the earliest delinquency is three years old. A payment plan may keep an owner out of escalated collection.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Multnomah County house with taxes still owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays the taxes and interest out of your proceeds. Ask the county for a payoff figure and give it to the title company.
